class_id: one status value means both 'queued' and 'impossible', so a permanently-unprocessable row is indistinguishable from a waiting one
feature: any pipeline that admits work into a queue before checking whether a processor for that work KIND exists — document extraction, job runners, import pipelines, message handlers with a type-dispatched consumer
symptom: the writer admits a row and stamps it with the queue's initial status (PENDING / QUEUED / NEW). The consumer dispatches on a TYPE field against a hard-coded set of handlers, and silently skips any type not in that set. A row whose type has no handler is therefore admitted, stamped PENDING, skipped on every pass, and stays PENDING forever — while a row whose type DOES have a handler is PENDING only until the next pass. One status value now covers two populations with opposite futures: 'will be processed shortly' and 'can never be processed'. Every count, dashboard, backlog metric and alert built on that status silently merges them, so the permanent population looks like transient load and the transient population looks chronically stuck. The shape is worse than a plain backlog because it is self-concealing: adding processing capacity, draining the queue faster, or building a second-pass walker moves the first population and leaves the second exactly where it was, which reads as 'the drain did not work'. The generic test is: partition the queue by whether a handler exists for the row's type, and check whether the no-handler partition is 100% in the initial state — if it is, the status is carrying two meanings.
first_seen: 2026-09-20 — IPODhan `documents`, measured read-only on ipodhan_staging through the sanctioned tunnel while building item 17. 155 documents sit extraction_status='PENDING'. Partitioned by whether the type is in EXTRACTABLE_DOC_TYPES (PRICE_BAND_AD, RHP, DRHP, PROSPECTUS) plus ANCHOR_DOC_TYPE (ANCHOR_ALLOCATION_REPORT, its own extractor and write door): 90 documents on 85 IPOs HAVE an extractor; 65 documents on 43 IPOs have NONE. The no-extractor population is 100% PENDING — 65 of 65, zero COMPLETED, zero FAILED, across every status the table holds — which is the signature of the class rather than a coincidence of load: a type that is sometimes processed would show a mix. It is also still being written: oldest 2026-06-18, NEWEST 2026-09-17 (three days before measurement), so this is an open tap and not a historical backlog, whereas the has-extractor population stopped arriving 2026-06-18. The types are RATIOS_BASIS_ISSUE_PRICE (43), SAMPLE_APPLICATION_FORMS (6), SECURITY_PARAMS_PRE_ANCHOR (6), SECURITY_PARAMS_POST_ANCHOR (3), BIDDING_CENTERS (3), CORRIGENDUM (2), BASIS_OF_ALLOTMENT_AD (1), ADDENDUM (1). The measurement was prompted by item 17, whose build card and issue #717 both frame the backlog as '74 stuck PROSPECTUS documents' — true, and 42% of the PENDING rows are a different problem that item 17's second-pass walker cannot touch, because a second visit to a document with no extractor produces the same nothing as the first.
fix_prs: none yet — registered as a finding while building item 17 (PR #868), which deliberately does NOT address it and says so in its commit body. The remedy is NOT to build eight extractors. It is to stop one value carrying two meanings, cheapest first: (1) at admission, a document whose type has no registered extractor is stamped with a terminal, honest status (NOT_EXTRACTABLE / NO_EXTRACTOR) rather than PENDING — the check is a set membership against the same constant the consumer dispatches on, so the two cannot drift; (2) the existing 65 rows are migrated to that status by a re-runnable, source-backed tool, dry-run by default; (3) only then is 'which of these types is worth an extractor' a separate, sized product question, answerable because the count is finally honest. Ordering matters: building an extractor first would shrink the number and leave the class intact for the ninth type.
detection_check: none yet. The check that would catch the next member is generic and cheap: for every distinct documents.type, report the share of rows in extraction_status='PENDING' older than N days, and FAIL when a type is 100% PENDING with a non-zero count — that is the no-handler signature, and it fires on the NINTH type the day it first appears rather than after a quarter of accumulation. It must partition by TYPE, never report a single PENDING total, because the single total is precisely what hid this for three months. The same shape generalises to any type-dispatched consumer: enumerate the handler set from the consumer's own dispatch constant (not a hand-kept list, which drifts) and assert every admitted type is in it.
